understanding: The bridge runs TWO distinct, weakly-connected audit systems. (1) A runtime SENSOR auditor (lib/auditor.ps1): every ~15min when idle it builds Get-AuditorSnapshot, runs deterministic triggers (commit_famine, wait_state_stuck, empty_reply_streak, same_task_too_long, critic_pingpong, working_tree_drift, restart_frequency, doctor_recidivism), then a cheap LLM (gemini-2.5-flash-lite) classifies normal|transient|hung|corrupted_state|unsolvable and Dispatch-AuditorVerdict activates Doctor / notifies / suppresses. It feeds Doctor, NOT the backlog. (2) A nightly CODE-FINDING audit (driver/10-maintenance.ps1 Start-AuditIfDue, window 01-06, once-per-window-occurrence, floor 20h, maxWait 60, launch-admission 2/60min) -> tools/audit.ps1 Invoke-BridgeAudit runs static security+functional subcomponents, a Start-Job signal collector (30s), then the DEEP phase: Invoke-DeepAuditProcess spawns tools/deep-audit.ps1 as a child PowerShell (Start-Process + $proc.WaitForExit + $proc.Kill on timeout -> status deep_failed), which in Invoke-MultiAgentDeepAudit fans out up to maxParallelAgents(3) per-role agents (tools/deep-audit-agent.ps1: 8 roles security/functional/reliability/architecture/dependency/runtime-incident/latency/cost), plus codex.exe + claude.exe passes, with quorum minSuccess=ceil(N/2) and required slices that never abort. Findings flow: agents -> Get-DeepAuditDedupedFindings -> Update-FindingsLedger (rootCauseKey state machine) -> Add-Idea (-SkipCurator) -> Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate -> approved/held/deduped/dropped -> backlog -> held-auto-triage / reaper / workpack -> driver claims -> fix. Efficiency = real problems fixed / real problems present. The funnel loses yield at every hop, but the decisive break is that nothing closes the loop back to the ledger.
summary:
PROJECT_MAP (audit efficiency funnel, by layer):
L0 INPUTS  - source files (capped reads), telemetry (turns/usage/restarts/circuit-breaker), runtime state.json.
L1 DETECT  - static subcomponents + 8 deep LLM agents + codex/claude; runtime sensor auditor (separate).
L2 DEDUP/AGE - Get-DeepAuditDedupedFindings (per-run) + Update-FindingsLedger (cross-run rootCauseKey: new/open/fixed/suppressed/regressed).
L3 GATE    - Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate (dedup vs open, security-evidence verify, file-existence).
L4 QUEUE   - Add-Idea -> approved(bridge)/held(project); held-auto-triage, state-reaper, workpack pressure.
L5 FIX     - driver claims approved items, edits, commits, QA.
L6 FEEDBACK- usefulness.jsonl (action_rate, resolved_signal_delta, incident_capture_rate); ledger close-out.

CHAPTERS FOR OPERATOR REVIEW:
Ch.1 Close the audit->fix loop (L6/L2): CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE - in production, ledger state 'fixed' is only READ (audit.ps1:620); the only writer Update-FindingsLedger emits new/open/regressed. Findings never close, so resolved_signal_delta ~ 0, regressed-detection is dead, usefulness structurally cannot see fix-rate, and fixed findings re-file or sit falsely-open. This is why 'доходимость до фикса' is both LOW and INVISIBLE. Fix: on backlog-item completion+QA-pass, set the originating finding's ledger entry to 'fixed' (id linkage already exists via Add-Idea return).
Ch.2 Deep-LLM reliability (pain #1, RELEVANCE CHECK): the stated 'Start-Job/Stop-Job hung socket' is now mostly STALE - the live agent path is Start-Process + WaitForExit + Kill (deep-audit.ps1 Start/Complete-DeepAuditAgentProcess), only the signal collector still uses Start-Job/Stop-Job(30s). Real residual root causes of deep_failed agents=0: (a) $proc.Kill() is NOT a tree-kill on Windows -> orphan grandchildren (codex/claude/LLM sockets) survive; (b) outer DeepAuditTimeoutSec watchdog kills the orchestrator and DISCARDS all partial agent results (no incremental result write); (c) Invoke-LLM lacks confirmed hard wall-clock cancellation, so a wedged socket consumes the whole budget -> missing_output_file.
Ch.3 Gate precision/recall (pain #3): non-security findings with any existing-file token are auto-APPROVED with zero content verification (backlog-workpack.ps1:640) while prose-only findings are HELD into limbo. Security path is well-verified; the rest is not.
Ch.4 Coverage (pain #2): per-role agents read capped content (security 5000, reliability 10000, default 20000 chars) -> large core files (server.ps1/driver.ps1) are mostly UNSEEN; runtime incidents the sensor auditor already catches never become durable findings.
Ch.5 Staleness & cadence (pains #4/#5): -SkipCurator on audit findings bypasses the freshness/auto-resolved check, so stale audit tasks get worked; once-nightly + maxWait 60 can be skipped entirely on busy nights -> up to 24h+ detection latency.

This plan strengthens existing mechanisms only (Foundation #2): the ledger state machine, the watchdog/kill, the intake gate, usefulness scoring, the freshness check, and the file-cap policy - no new subsystems.

decision_atoms.statement: P1 - Close the ledger loop: mark a finding 'fixed' when the backlog item derived from it completes with a QA pass. Reuse the existing Add-Idea->item id linkage, the existing qa_verdict_cache/post-commit QA signal, and Update-FindingsLedger; add a single close-out call on task completion that flips the matching rootCauseKey to 'fixed'.
decision_atoms.reason: Confirmed: no production code ever sets ledger state 'fixed' (audit.ps1:620 is read-only). This silently zeroes resolved_signal_delta, kills regressed-detection, makes usefulness blind to fix-rate, and causes fixed findings to re-file or sit open forever. Closing this is the single highest-leverage change for the headline metric (share of real problems actually fixed) because it both raises true yield and finally makes the metric observable.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Risk of false-closing a finding if a commit touches the file without truly fixing it; mitigated by requiring (a) the specific originating backlog item completed AND (b) a QA pass, scoped by item id, not 'any commit to the file'.

decision_atoms.statement: P2 - Make the deep phase loss-resilient: have deep-audit.ps1 write its result JSON incrementally (per agent as it completes) so audit.ps1's Invoke-DeepAuditProcess reads whatever finished even when the outer watchdog fires, instead of recording deep_failed agents=0.
decision_atoms.reason: Today a single slow/wedged agent can push total runtime past DeepAuditTimeoutSec; the outer Kill() then discards ALL agent output, producing the exact reported symptom (static gives findings, deep gives 0). Persisting partial results converts a total loss into graceful degradation and recovers most of the deep yield on bad nights.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slightly more file I/O and a marginally more complex result contract between deep-audit.ps1 and audit.ps1; both already exchange a result file, so the surface is small.

decision_atoms.statement: P3 - Replace bare $proc.Kill() with a scoped process-TREE kill for both the deep orchestrator and each agent, and verify/repair Invoke-LLM hard wall-clock cancellation; if Invoke-LLM cannot guarantee cancellation, wrap its socket call with a hard timeout.
decision_atoms.reason: On Windows $proc.Kill() terminates only the immediate child, leaving codex.exe/claude.exe/LLM HTTP sockets as orphans that keep consuming handles and can wedge the next run. The original pain (Start-Job/Stop-Job not breaking a hung socket) is now mostly stale, but the underlying disease - no tree-kill + no hard socket cancellation - is still present and is the true root of hung deep runs.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Tree-kill must be scoped to the captured spawn PID-set (job object / child-PID list) so it never kills a codex/claude process shared by other bridge work; needs careful PID capture at spawn time.

decision_atoms.statement: P4 - Strengthen Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate to content-verify ALL categories, not just security: reuse Get-BacklogIntakeReferencedLines to require that the cited line/symbol actually exists before auto-approving a non-security finding, and rescue prose-only findings by re-deriving a file hint before holding.
decision_atoms.reason: Currently any finding that merely names an existing file is approved unverified (backlog-workpack.ps1:640), so plausible-but-wrong functional/architecture findings reach the work queue (wasted fix cycles = lost efficiency), while genuinely real findings described in prose are dumped to 'held'. Extending the already-built evidence check raises precision AND recall simultaneously.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: More findings land in 'held' initially, increasing operator-escalation volume; mitigated by the existing held-auto-triage and by attaching the concrete evidence so triage is fast.

decision_atoms.statement: P5 - Stratify file-content caps and window large core files: raise/segment the cap for priority-1 files (server.ps1, driver.ps1, supervisor.ps1) in Get-AgentFileContentCapped/Get-AgentRiskRankedFiles so they are audited in overlapping windows rather than truncated at 5000 chars.
decision_atoms.reason: The biggest, highest-risk files are exactly the ones most truncated, so most of their body is invisible to the per-role agents - a structural coverage hole (pain #2). Audited content is the precondition for any finding to exist at all.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: More tokens and latency per run; bounded by chunking only the handful of priority-1 core files and keeping a per-run token budget.

decision_atoms.statement: P6 - Upgrade Write-AuditUsefulnessScore to per-slice filed->fixed conversion (enabled by P1) and auto-demote chronically unfixed slices: a slice that files steadily but whose findings are essentially never fixed gets its model downgraded or that slice paused.
decision_atoms.reason: Efficiency is a closed-loop control problem; today usefulness measures only filing (action_rate) and a dead resolved-delta. Once P1 makes fix-rate observable, feeding it back to throttle low-yield slices directly optimizes the metric and cuts noise/cost.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Risk of demoting a slice that is valuable but slow-to-fix (e.g. security); mitigate by exempting required slices and using a long observation window before any demotion.

decision_atoms.statement: P7 - Promote runtime incidents the sensor auditor already classifies (corrupted_state / repeated unsolvable) into durable deduped findings via the existing Add-Idea path, instead of only notifying main and activating Doctor.
decision_atoms.reason: The two audit systems are disjoint: the runtime auditor detects real, reproducible problems but they evaporate after a chat notice unless the nightly runtime-incident-model agent independently re-derives them. Routing operator-visible auditor verdicts into the same finding pipeline closes a detection->durable-fix gap with no new mechanism.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Could add backlog noise if auditor classification is jittery; mitigated by filing only the stable operator-visible classes and going through the same intake gate + dedup.

decision_atoms.statement: P8 - Run the cheap freshness/auto-resolved check for audit findings even though they use -SkipCurator: keep the LLM curator off (cost) but execute the deterministic freshness-skip so a finding already addressed by a later commit is auto-resolved before it is claimed.
decision_atoms.reason: -SkipCurator currently skips the whole curator, including the freshness-skip handled in Publish-CuratorDecisionEvents, so stale audit tasks get worked - a direct waste that lowers effective fix-yield (pain #5). Decoupling the deterministic freshness check from the costly curator LLM keeps cost flat while preventing stale work.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Small extra per-item check at intake; must ensure the freshness check itself is cheap/deterministic and does not reintroduce curator latency.

decision_atoms.statement: P9 - Add a window catch-up guard in Start-AuditIfDue so a nightly audit that was skipped (system busy past 06:00, never reached stable idle) still runs opportunistically once the last SUCCESSFUL audit exceeds floorHours, rather than waiting a full day.
decision_atoms.reason: Once-nightly + maxWait 60 means a busy night silently skips detection entirely, pushing detection latency past 24h and starving the whole funnel (pain #4). Anchoring on last-successful (already partly modeled by floorHours) closes the skip without a new scheduler.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: A daytime catch-up audit competes with live work for idle and tokens; bound it to a strict floor and the existing launch-admission limiter.

assumptions: I reviewed the master tree; worktrees/parallel/0ebb429fa86d/A/* is another proposer's isolated copy and was ignored.

No production path sets ledger state 'fixed'/'suppressed' - inferred from grep (only audit.ps1:620 reads them; only test-findings-ledger.ps1 writes them) and from Update-FindingsLedger emitting only new/open/regressed. Should be re-verified against any reflect.ps1 / librarian / backlog-completion hook before implementing P1.
Invoke-LLM (lib) does not currently enforce a hard wall-clock cancellation on a wedged socket; I did not open lib/llm.* and this must be confirmed before P3.
Add-Idea returns an item id that can be persisted on the originating ledger entry to link finding<->backlog item for P1 close-out (the return value is already captured as $bid in audit.ps1).
The post-commit QA signal (qa_verdict_cache in state, Test-AuditorQaCachePass) is reliable enough to gate a 'fixed' transition.
DISCUSS mode: this is a plan for operator review; nothing here is to be implemented in this task.

risks.risk: P1 false-closes a finding: a commit touches the file without actually fixing the issue, ledger marks it 'fixed', and the real problem is hidden until regression.
risks.mitigation: Gate the 'fixed' transition on the SPECIFIC originating backlog item completing AND a QA pass, scoped by item id; leave regressed-detection (already present) to re-open it on the next audit if it reappears.

risks.risk: P3 tree-kill terminates a codex.exe/claude.exe process shared by other bridge work, causing collateral failures.
risks.mitigation: Capture the exact child PID-set / use a Windows job object at spawn time and kill only that scoped tree; never kill by image name. Stage behind a config flag and the -Sequential debug path first.

risks.risk: P4 content-verification raises the 'held' rate, flooding the operator with escalations and slowing real fixes.
risks.mitigation: Attach concrete evidence (referenced lines) to each held item so held-auto-triage and the operator resolve fast; keep criticals surfaced; tune thresholds on usefulness.jsonl before full rollout.

risks.risk: Changing the deep result contract (P2 incremental writes) breaks audit.ps1's parser and yields deep_failed for a different reason.
risks.mitigation: Keep the final single-line JSON contract as-is and ADD incremental sidecar files that audit.ps1 reads only when the watchdog fires; cover with test-findings-ledger-style unit tests before enabling.

risks.risk: P6 auto-demotion silences a slow-but-valuable slice (e.g. security) because real fixes take longer than the observation window.
risks.mitigation: Exempt required slices from demotion; require a long, multi-run window of zero fixes AND non-zero filing before any model downgrade; never fully disable, only downgrade the model tier.

risks.risk: Over-scoping: trying all nine atoms at once destabilizes a system that is currently at least producing static findings.
risks.mitigation: Ship in the phased order below; P1 is independently valuable and low-blast-radius (write-only ledger transition) and should land and be measured first.

minimal_version: Phase 1 (highest yield, lowest blast radius): implement P1 (close the ledger loop - mark findings 'fixed' on linked-item completion + QA pass) and P2 (incremental deep-result persistence so a watchdog kill no longer zeroes deep findings). These two alone (a) make fix-rate observable for the first time, (b) stop fixed findings re-filing, and (c) recover most deep yield on bad nights. Validate by watching audit/usefulness.jsonl resolved_signal_delta become non-zero and deep_failed-with-agents=0 frequency drop. No new mechanisms - only Update-FindingsLedger, the existing QA signal, and the existing deep result file are touched.
advanced_version: Phase 2: P3 (scoped tree-kill + Invoke-LLM hard cancellation) and P4 (content-verify all intake-gate categories) - hardens reliability and precision/recall together. Phase 3: P5 (stratified caps for core files) + P7 (promote runtime-auditor incidents into durable findings) - closes coverage holes. Phase 4: P6 (per-slice filed->fixed feedback + auto-demotion of unfixed slices), P8 (deterministic freshness check despite -SkipCurator), P9 (window catch-up) - turns the funnel into a measured closed-loop controller that continuously optimizes share-of-real-problems-fixed and trims noise/cost. Each phase is independently shippable, reversible behind config, and strengthens an existing component rather than adding one (Foundation #2).
